reason: The one window-wide drop listener: a file dropped where no surface takes it would make Chromium navigate to it. Surfaces bind their own drop zone (a workbench slot), which fires first.
The keybind dispatcher. A keybind is a global gesture by definition; which surface answers it is the registry's decision (`CommandOwner`), not the listener's.
Pane chords, Escape during a pane drag, and the forward of an unhandled key to the shown surface of the focused pane — the router every surface's `PaneCtx.onKeyDown` goes through.
Stands in for a workbench slot while there is no content; it is the only surface on screen, so its `PaneCtx.onKeyDown` binds to `document` directly.
The review panel is the workbench for its subagent session tabs: this host hands each one a PaneCtx whose onKeyDown binds to document and forwards only while that tab is the shown one.
Hold-modifier tab switcher; one instance in the shell.
Records the next chord while the recorder is open; a modal affordance with no rival.

Module-level singleton tracking whether cmd/ctrl is held so link decorations match what a click would do; not per terminal, writes no surface state. Could read the modifier off the pointer event instead.
Escape leaves inspect mode. Lives in the workspace panel, not a workbench slot; gated by its own inspect state. Debt: bind to the pane root, which can hold focus while inspecting.
`d` toggles diff style. Lives in the workspace panel, not a workbench slot; guards itself with a `#review-panel` rect check because it listens too broadly. Debt: register as a command.
Extends the search query after focus deliberately leaves the input, only while its popover is open; a hidden slot cannot open the popover.
